tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
a) Dice Similarity Coefficient (Dice)
b) Hausdorff distance (HD)

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

1) Dice Similarity Coefficient (Dice): Dice is used to evaluate the area-based overlap index.
2) Hausdorff distance (HD): HD is used to evaluate the coincidence of the surface for stability and sensitivity to
outliers.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

1) Calculate the Dice, HD for all cases.
2) Rank the Dice, HD separately.
3) Rank average score as final task score.
4) Tie if the scores are equal.


Extra Overall Ranking:
1)Rank average score of three tasks, unsubmitted tasks would be calculated as 0.
2)Tie if the scores are equal.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Report errors and teams need to help the participant to complete the missing results in the first time. Incomplete
submissions will be scored as 0.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

This ranking scheme is developed to take important metrics into account separately in each task, and also evaluate
overall performance of participants among three tasks. In segmentation and classification task, it evaluates two
metrics to prevent bias. And it asserts detection task performance with a relatively strict metric.

properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
a)Balanced accuracy
b)F1 score
c)Area under curve (AUC)

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

Since the dataset is not balanced, balanced accuracy, F1-score and AUC are adopted to evaluate performance of
model.
1) Balanced Accuracy: Balanced accuracy takes both sensitivity and specificity into consideration.
2) F1 Score: F1 score takes both recall and precision into consideration.
3) AUC: AUC provides an aggregate measure of performance across all possible classification thresholds.
